title: AI Cut Our Research Time From 7 Days to 15 Minutes — Gareth Yoder, Vanguard
talk_summary: A Vanguard tech lead describes exposing a legacy mainframe codebase and migration docs to AI tooling via an MCP server, collapsing a 7-day research loop to 15 minutes and cutting producer-support chats. The rest is migration/observability practice (CDC audits, idempotency, schema registry, business-case metadata) with light AI framing.

takeaways.technique: Expose internal knowledge/codebase as an MCP server
takeaways.what_they_do: They put the legacy codebase and wiki docs behind an MCP server so any AI tool can query them directly instead of routing questions through human experts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we had our legacy codebase being available to our AI tooling via an MCP server

takeaways.what_they_do: Engineers' product knowledge is written into common storage accessible to all team members and agents, so a new engineer's prompt has the same context as a 5-year veteran.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that knowledge goes into a common storage where it's now accessible by all members on the team

takeaways.what_they_do: They require each consumer to supply a description and business-case justification, then let AI compile those into accurate summaries of what's modernized and top functionality.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we requested that our consumers would provide us a description and a business case justification for their need for the data

takeaways.technique: Row-count then column-level audit for data parity
takeaways.what_they_do: Daily audits first verify row-level counts for consistency, then check individual columns for integrity between legacy and modern stores.
takeaways.evidence_quote: verifying the row level data counts, and then we ensured that we had strong integrity by checking the individual columns

takeaways.what_they_do: They carry idempotency from producers through event streaming so failed batch jobs can retry without creating duplicate ledgers.

takeaways.technique: Impact-tiered SLAs tied to business use case
takeaways.what_they_do: They attach business justification to each app so during incidents they know whether a breach means hours (batch) or minutes (real-time) to respond.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A batch application we may have hours to respond. A real-time API where there's a client on the other side
